extraction.name: Geometry3K
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark consisting of 3,002 geometry problems with dense annotation in formal language, collected from two popular high-school textbooks. Each problem includes problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, correct answer, problem goal, and geometry shapes. Problems are annotated with formal language descriptions for both text and diagrams using 91 predicates.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu
extraction.citeAs: Lu, P., Gong, R., Jiang, S., Qiu, L., Huang, S., Liang, X., & Zhu, S.-C. (2021). Inter-GPS: Interpretable Geometry Problem Solving with Formal Language and Symbolic Reasoning. arXiv:2105.04165v3 [cs.CL].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data is collected from two popular textbooks for high school students across grades 6-12 by two online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline). Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collect each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer. Each problem is further labeled with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes, and annotated with dense formal language descriptions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Geometry problems from two online digital libraries: McGraw-Hill (https://www.mheducation.com/) and Geometryonline (www.geometryonline.com), covering high school textbooks for grades 6-12.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset is divided into train, validation, and test sets with the ratio of 0.7:0.1:0.2, resulting in 2,101 training, 300 validation, and 601 test problems.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each problem is annotated with formal language descriptions for both text and diagrams. Problem text is parsed via rule-based text parsing using regular expressions. Diagrams are parsed using Hough Transformation to extract geometry primitives (points, lines, arcs, circles), followed by neural object detection with RetinaNet for diagram symbols and text regions, and optical character recognition with MathPix for textual content.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually annotated each problem with problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, correct answer, problem goal, and geometry shapes. Each problem is further annotated with dense formal language descriptions for both text and diagrams using a defined set of 91 predicates. Human performance was evaluated by pushing test-split data to Amazon Mechanical Turk, where each eligible annotator must have obtained a high school or higher degree and answered 10 problems in 25 minutes, spending at least 7 minutes on the problem set and 10 seconds on each problem. Human expert performance was evaluated by asking dozens of graduates majoring in science or engineering to answer the problems.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (for human performance evaluation)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotators who did not satisfy the time requirements (at least 7 minutes on the problem set and 10 seconds on each problem) were filtered out. Human overall accuracy was 56.9% and human expert accuracy was 90.9%, compared to random guess accuracy of 25%.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees for data collection; Amazon Mechanical Turk workers with high school or higher degree for human performance evaluation; dozens of graduates majoring in science or engineering for human expert evaluation.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Hough Transformation for geometry primitive extraction; RetinaNet neural object detector for diagram symbol and text region extraction; MathPix OCR tool for textual content recognition in diagrams; BART (sequence-to-sequence model) for semantic text parsing comparison.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and evaluation baselines are released to promote follow-up work in the geometry domain. Available at https://lupantech.github.io/inter-gps.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work may inspire following research in symbolic reasoning and interpretable models and facilitate education. Solving geometry problems is an essential subject in high-school education for the development of students' abstract thinking.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is collected from two specific online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline), which may limit diversity. The problems are SAT-style and cover grades 6-12, which may not represent all geometry problem types or educational systems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current neural network baselines fail to achieve satisfactory results due to limited data samples. The diagram parser still has significant room for improvement (17.5% gap between predicted and ground truth diagram literals). The symbolic solver is not capable of solving complex problems with combined shapes and shaded areas. Text parser has difficulty handling nested expressions and uncertain references. Diagram parsing tends to fail with ambiguous annotations or multiple primitives.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of geometry problem solving algorithms. The dataset is particularly suited for symbolic reasoning and interpretable problem solving. It can be used to evaluate fine-grained performance of geometry solvers across different problem types (angle, length, area, ratio, line, triangle, quadrilateral, circle).
